checkedAlternates.risk: Most supermarket yogurt is sweetened, so yogurt reads as sweet to many players.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The label says plain yogurt, whose dominant taste is sour; the sweet row is already full with four unambiguous items.

checkedAlternates.risk: Coffee is usually drunk with sugar, which can pull it toward sweet.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The label says black coffee, and bitter is the only taste in the set with a single representative.

checkedAlternates.risk: Berry jams keep a tart edge, so jam can read as sour.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Sugar dominates jam by weight and by taste; the sour row is filled by lemon, vinegar and plain yogurt.

checkedAlternates.risk: Dark soy sauce carries a bitter note alongside the salt.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Salt is what soy sauce is used for, and the salty row has no other candidate besides salt itself.

authorReview.notes: Two item labels were written defensively — "black coffee" and "plain yogurt" — precisely because the bare words would have been ambiguous.

blindPlaytest.notes: If testers still read plain yogurt as sweet, swap it for pickles.
